control_device_fabrication: Based on a systematically tuned set of experimental parameters, this perovskite solar cell was meticulously prepared, ultimately achieving a PCE of 17.059%, FF of 78.585%, Voc of 1.0245 V, and Jsc of 21.189 mA/cm². The 1.73 mol/L perovskite solution (Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1) was prepared, shaken overnight to fully dissolve, and then used to prepare perovskite films. For the SAM solution, Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL) was added to the previous solution.  A two-tier spin-coating strategy (1000 rpm/10 s and 5000 rpm/30 s) produced a uniform and defect-minimized perovskite layer. 160 µL CB was dripped onto the center of film at 6 s before the end of spin-coating. Subsequently, the sample was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
target_device_fabrication: Remarkably, it achieved an impressive PCE of 17.6476% with a high VOC of 1.0462 V, JSC of 22.8308 mA/cm², and FF of 73.884%. The composition of perovskite is 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1. The optimal SAM was prepared by using Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL).The sample of Me-4PACz was fabricated with a concentration of 0.33 mg/mL. MACl (with 9.5 mg/mL) additive was incorporated. The perovskite precursor solution was dripped onto substrate, and a two-step spin-coating procedure was applied. The first step was carried out at 1000 rpm, followed by 5000 rpm for 30 s. 160 µL CB as antisolvent was dropped 6 s before the end of the spin-coating procedure. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 25 min for perovskite crystal formation.
